newsitem.title: INDIA: Calcutta shares close lower as foreign funds sell.
newsitem.headline: Calcutta shares close lower as foreign funds sell.

text.p: Calcutta shares, hit by fresh selling pressure, ended lower on Wednesday with most foreign and local mutual funds liquidating even blue-chips, brokers said.
They said volumes slumped to low levels. The Calcutta index closed 3.24 points down at 439.66.
Brokers said that even though selling may not have been in large lots, it was the absence of any buying which pushed most pivotals down.
"I perceive the market to turn worse. There is nothing positive for investors to look forward for," said stock analyst Mathew Easow.

"There is a massive shift of funds into the debt market from equities. With debt instruments offering interest rates as high as 20 percent per annum, something which equities does not promise, the equity market can only suffer from a liquidity crisis," Easow said.

Brokers said that even though today was the first day of accounting period at the National Stock Exchange (NSE), Bombay traders did not place any orders with their Calcutta counterparts resulting in low volumes and lower prices.
